rationale: 3x3 blocks reduce 6x12 to 2x4; in demonstration 1, the lower-left block has five zeros and four threes and outputs 0.
Each vertical pair becomes one cell; demonstration 2 maps [2,0] to 5 and [0,0] to 0.
3x3 blocks reduce 9x12 to 3x4; demonstration 1's upper-right block contains three threes and six zeros but outputs 3, ignoring background.
2x2 blocks reduce 8x8 to 4x4; demonstration 1 maps a block with three ones to 1 and the upper-right block with two zeros and two ones to 0.
Horizontal pairs become 5 whenever occupied; demonstration 2 maps [0,3] and [0,1] to 5, while [0,0] becomes 0.
Vertical pairs retain the non-background colour; demonstration 2 maps [3,0] to 3 and [0,1] to 1.
Each occupied 2x2 block becomes 5; demonstration 1's bottom-right block has a single 2 and outputs 5, while empty blocks output 0.
Each 2x2 block selects its most common non-background colour; demonstration 1's middle-row third block has one 3 and three zeros and outputs 3.
2x3 blocks reduce 6x6 to 3x2; demonstration 1 maps four ones and two zeros to 1, and three twos tied with three zeros to 0.
Horizontal pairs select the non-background colour; demonstration 2 maps [1,0] to 1, [2,0] to 2, and [0,3] to 3.
